IGUI_GTPG_HowItWorks:
There are six vitamins: A, B, C, D, E and K. Each has a Reserve from 0 to %1. Below %2 it is Critical, below %3 Low, otherwise Sufficient.
Every day each vitamin's Reserve drops by %4.
Eating food adds Reserve. Eating a whole day's need of a vitamin gives +%5. Eating half a food gives half.
Every %6 Reserve you gain banks 1 pause day. A day with a banked pause day uses it up instead of dropping, and that vitamin's deficiency effects stay quiet. Eat well every day and you stay ahead.
When a vitamin falls below %2 its deficiency starts. The effects stay until the Reserve is back up to %3, not just out of Critical, like a real deficiency.
Stale or rotten food gives fewer vitamins. Vitamins follow how much hunger the food still fills.
Your character also mentions how they feel now and then while something is short.
IGUI_GTPG_EffectsOn: Deficiency effects are on in this world (the Vitamins tab says what each one does). On top of those, each vitamin in deficiency lowers your highest Endurance by 10 percent, and this stacks: three vitamins short = at most 70 percent.

IGUI_GTPG_Other_Pills_Body:
Taking vitamin pills (a vanilla item) gives every vitamin +1 pause day: for about a day nothing drops and deficiency effects are quiet. It does not raise the Reserve. It is relief, not a cure, so you still need to eat.
Make them (Medical, keep a mortar and pestle): 1 empty jar, 1 salt, and one of each: carrot / sweet potato / pumpkin; egg / beef / chicken / pork / venison / rabbit; bell pepper / tomato / orange / lemon; salmon / fish fillet / milk; peanuts / soybeans; broccoli / cabbage / spinach.
IGUI_GTPG_Other_Cooking_Body: Stews, soups and other pot or pan dishes keep the vitamins of everything you put in, by how much of each went in. Eating part of the dish gives that part. Mixing vegetables, meat and fish in one pot covers many vitamins at once.
IGUI_GTPG_Other_Fresh_Body: Vitamins follow how much hunger a food still fills. When food goes stale or rotten the game lowers that, and the vitamins drop with it. Eat produce fresh, keep it cold, or can it.
IGUI_GTPG_Other_NotTracked_Body: Milk and anything else you drink from a container, candy and snacks, herbs, spices and seeds. Canned condensed milk (a solid food) does count. A food not in the All foods tab gives no vitamins.

IGUI_GTPG_Other_Grow_Title: Grow your own fruit (Fruit Farming by leina)
IGUI_GTPG_Other_Grow_Body:
"Fruit Farming (B42)" by leina is built into this mod, with thanks. Now every vitamin can be farmed, not only scavenged.
1. Collect seeds: a knife (or tweezers) and a fruit. Apple, pear, orange, lemon, lime and grapefruit give 3 seeds. Cherry, olive and grapes give 2. Avocado, mango, peach, banana and pineapple give 1. The recipes are under Farming.
2. Plant the seeds in a dug furrow and water them, like any vanilla seed. Each crop has its own sowing months. Apple, cherry, pear and coffee stand the cold; the others need the warm months. A crop takes about 80 to 110 days to bear.
3. Fruit trees, grape vines and coffee are perennial: after a harvest they go back a few stages and bear again.
4. Rice: collect seeds from a bag of rice, harvest with a scythe, dry the sheaves on a drying rack, thresh them, and put 12 seeds in a bag. Coffee: seeds from chocolate-covered coffee beans; dry the pods, roast them, then grind 12 at a stone quern. Ginger and peanuts: plant the root or the nut itself.
Tick Can grow next to the search box to list only foods you can grow.
IGUI_GTPG_Other_Tips_Body:
- D is the hardest one: fish (salmon is best), eggs, cheese, butter, mushrooms.
- B: meat, fish, beans and lentils, peanuts.
- A: carrots, sweet potatoes, leafy greens, butter, eggs, mangoes.
- C: bell peppers, oranges, pineapple, broccoli, brussels sprouts, rosehips.
- K: leafy greens such as kale, spinach, dandelions, grape leaves and brussels sprouts; avocados.
- E: olive or vegetable oil, nuts, avocado, beans, olives.
A vegetable garden, a few fruit trees, some fishing and eggs cover all six. Fruit for winter: can it while it is in season.
IGUI_GTPG_Tab_calendar_Tip: When to sow each crop, month by month. This month is marked.
IGUI_GTPG_CalOnlyFF: On a multiplayer client the game's own crop table is not loaded here, so only the fruit crops are listed. The plant info in the field still shows the season of every crop.
IGUI_GTPG_Other_Sun_Body: Like real skin in the sun, standing outside in daylight (9:00 to 16:59, not in rain) slowly gives vitamin D: %1 Reserve per game hour, at most %2 a day. Winter months give half. This is less than the daily drop of 5, so it helps but you still need fish, eggs, dairy or mushrooms. Admins can change it in the sandbox options.
IGUI_GTPG_Other_Dried_Body: Put apples, pears, peaches, mangoes, bananas, cherries, grapes or pineapple on a drying rack, the same rack used for grain. Dried fruit keeps for months and is as filling as the fresh fruit with the water gone. It keeps most of its vitamins, but drying loses over half the vitamin C. Grapes become raisins. Dried fruit goes into cakes, sweet pies, oatmeal, pancakes, muffins and fruit salad.
IGUI_GTPG_Other_Sprouts_Body:
1. Soak: a jar with a little water and some dried beans (lentils, chickpeas, split peas, black, kidney or white beans - only part of the bag is used) or dried soybeans / green peas make a Jar of Soaking Beans.
2. Wait about 2 to 3 days: it turns into a Jar of Bean Sprouts by itself (slower in a fridge).
3. Take the sprouts out: 4 bean sprouts and the jar back.
Fresh vitamin C and K in any season, even in winter, from a pantry. They go into salads, stir fries, soups, rice and pasta. Eat them within a few days.
IGUI_GTPG_Other_FishOil_Body: Cooking recipe: a pot or saucepan (kept), an empty jar and 4 fish guts (left over from filleting), fish fillets or salmon give a jar of fish liver oil. It is rich in vitamins A and D and keeps for weeks; the jar comes back when it is used up.
IGUI_GTPG_Other_Canning_Body:
Cooking recipe: 1 empty tin can + 4 of the same vegetable or fruit + 1 salt = a sealed home-canned jar. 41 kinds of produce work, lemons and limes included.
A sealed jar never spoils. Open it with a can opener. Once open it is fresh for 2 days and rotten after 4.
A jar holds the vitamins of 4 fresh pieces, so it is the way to keep summer vitamins for winter.
IGUI_GTPG_Tab_cook_Tip: Ready-made dishes cooked the vanilla way, with preparation minigames. Vitamins carry over from the ingredients.
IGUI_GTPC_Intro: Pick a dish on the left - about a hundred of them, from soups and stir fries to pies, pizza, toast and hot drinks. Every dish is one of the game's own cooking recipes; new ones unlock as your Cooking level rises. You prepare the ingredients step by step - wash, peel, chop, mash, grind, stir, season, steep - each a short minigame with the real tool you have in your hand (a knife, a fork for whisking, bare hands when nothing else will do - just harder). Ingredients are flexible: a slot takes its listed foods or any other food of that kind the game accepts. They go into the pot or pan exactly as when you add them by hand, so calories, carbohydrates, fat, protein, hunger and rotting stay the game's own, and every ingredient's vitamins pass into the dish by the hunger it gives. Better preparation makes the dish less boring and more satisfying and gives more Cooking XP. Finally cook it the usual way: on a lit stove, in an oven or over a campfire.

IGUI_GTPC_Hint_scale: Hold the mouse and scrape off every patch of scales.
IGUI_GTPC_Hint_spread: Hold the mouse and cover the whole slice evenly.
IGUI_GTPC_Hint_slice: Thin slices: click on each line as the knife passes.

IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_wash_1: Dirt off first. I'll scrub every spot until it's clean.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_wash_2: Under the water... rub each dirty patch away.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_scale_1: Scales off - scrape every patch, tail to head.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_scale_2: Scrape firmly over each patch of scales.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_peel_1: Peel it in one go round - start at the ringed spot, then follow on.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_peel_2: Thin peel, in order. Skip ahead and I'll cut too deep.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_spread_1: Spread it right to the edges, every corner.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_spread_2: Nice and even over the whole slice.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_chop_1: Wait for the knife over a line... then cut.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_chop_2: Steady hand. Cut right on each line.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_slice_1: Thin slices - click as the blade crosses each line.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_slice_2: Lots of thin cuts, keep the rhythm.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_mince_1: Fast and fine - hit every line as the cleaver passes.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_trim_1: Narrow cuts to trim the fat. Be exact.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_trim_2: Careful... only the bits that need to go.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_core_1: A few careful cuts around the core.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_core_2: Out with the pit - right on the line.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_crack_1: Tap it on the rim when the ring meets the bowl.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_crack_2: Not too hard, not too soft - no shell in the bowl!
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_knead_1: Push the dough each time the ring closes.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_knead_2: Fold and press, keep the beat.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_pound_1: Even blows each time the ring closes - makes it tender.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_pound_2: Flatten it out, on the beat.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_toss_1: Flick the pan when the ring closes - everything flips!
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_toss_2: Toss on the beat so nothing burns.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_flip_1: Watch it brown... flip when the bar is in the green. Twice.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_flip_2: Golden, not burnt - flip at the right moment.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_steep_1: Let it steep... take it out when the colour is just right.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_steep_2: Too short is weak, too long is bitter. Watch the colour.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_roll_1: Roll it out end to end, up and down.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_roll_2: Long even strokes with the pin.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_grate_1: Rub it up and down the grater - mind my knuckles.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_grate_2: Full strokes, stay on the grater.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_zest_1: Just the coloured skin - light strokes on the grater.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_zest_2: Gently... the white part is bitter.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_whisk_1: Fast circles, keep the speed in the green.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_stir_1: Slow, steady circles - don't splash it about.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_stir_2: Keep it moving so nothing sticks.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_fold_1: Gently fold it in - slow circles, keep the air in.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_grind_1: Grind it in the mortar at a steady pace.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_grind_2: Round and round till it's a paste.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_mash_2: No lumps left - squash them all!
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_season_1: Three pinches - stop in the green each time.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_season_2: A little at a time. You can't take salt back out.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_measure_1: Pour and stop right in the green band.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Tip_measure_2: Measure it properly - baking is exact.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Ev_Spill_1: It's flying out of the mortar!
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Ev_Deep_2: Not there yet - follow the order.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Ev_Dark_1: A bit dark on that side.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_End_Miss_1: That went wrong - let's try again.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Done_2: That's prepared. Into the heat it goes.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_DoneExcellent_1: Perfect prep - this one's going to be special.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Unlock_1: I think I could cook something new now.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_BuffOff_1: That good meal is wearing off.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_BuffOff_2: I could eat like that again.
IGUI_GTPC_BuffDesc_hearty: tire more slowly and get a little endurance back
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Buff_hearty_1: That'll keep me going for hours.
IGUI_GTPC_Say_Buff_calm_1: Warm and calm... I can breathe.
IGUI_GTPC_BuffDesc_fresh: a bit of endurance and good mood
